documents.unit: University Policy 3710.2: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct
documents.title: Academic Integrity Standards and Process for Misconduct (generative AI provisions)
documents.stance_why: Section 3710.2 sets a university default that bans AI: 'If an AI statement is not included in the course syllabus... students may not use any type of generative AI', yet it also says 'Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols... allowing or disallowing some or all use'. It sets a university-wide default ban that instructors can lift by syllabus statement, so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted, which is restrict. It is not delegates, because the silent-syllabus default is a binding ban with misconduct consequences, and it offers no tiers.
documents.summary: The generative-AI section (3710.2) of Wright State's academic-integrity policy defines generative AI, bans its use on coursework unless the syllabus or instructor permits it, and treats unauthorized use as an integrity violation. Instructors may allow or disallow use if they say so in the syllabus, and students who are unsure should ask. The rest of the policy is the general misconduct process and sanctions that AI cases follow.
